title: Click analytics goes offline
description: The click stream is unavailable for several minutes. Product says click counts are approximate, not billable, and redirects must stay fast. Your redirect service currently waits for a stream acknowledgement. Which policy best matches those requirements?

options.text: Write each click to the link database until the stream recovers.
options.explanation: This moves the analytics dependency onto the transactional database and still makes a redirect wait for an analytics write.

options.text: Keep every pending click in an unbounded in-memory queue.
options.explanation: A long outage can exhaust memory and take down redirects. Approximate counts do not justify that availability risk.

options.text: Return an error when the stream is down so clients retry the click later.
options.explanation: This sacrifices the required user path to protect optional analytics. Retrying also makes click counting harder.

options.text: Return the redirect immediately, buffer events asynchronously within a fixed limit, and drop overflow with monitoring.
options.explanation: The bounded buffer absorbs short outages without risking memory exhaustion. Dropping overflow is an explicit loss policy that fits approximate counts; billable clicks would need stronger durability.
